questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code pages through a user's notifications? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does page_for_user query limit + 1 rows and then slice to limit?
choices: To make sure the first page is never empty when the user has any notifications.
To learn whether another page exists without a separate COUNT query, and to build the cursor from the last row actually returned.
To compensate for the cursor row itself being included in the next page's results.
To keep a spare row available in case one of the rows is filtered out after loading.

questions.prompt: While a client is paging through its inbox, new notifications are inserted with a later created_at than anything the client has seen. How does this affect the pages the client still has to fetch?
choices: Every later page shifts by the number of new rows, so the client sees some notifications twice.
The client's next request fails with an invalid cursor because the data changed.
The remaining pages skip a few rows, because the new rows push older ones past the limit.
The remaining pages are unaffected; the new rows sort before the cursor position and only appear on a fresh first-page request.

questions.prompt: A client calls the endpoint with limit=1000 and a valid cursor. What does it receive?
choices: At most 100 items, and a next_cursor if more rows remain after those.
A 422 validation error, because 1000 exceeds the maximum page size.
Up to 1000 items, because MAX_PAGE_SIZE is only used when no limit is supplied.
At most 100 items, and next_cursor is always null because the requested limit was not honoured.
